source: Hand-traced from hdb-3room.webp (Task 17): every door, window and passage of the plan, on the walls of hdb-3room.drawing-walls.json.

method.convention: Each opening lies on one truth wall ('wall'), over [u0, u1] source px along it from the wall's node a toward b. 'hinge' is the jamb the leaf turns on (start = u0) and 'swing' the side it opens to (left = +n with n = (d.y, -d.x), d = the wall's a->b direction; 04 §2.1). kind: door (a swing arc, or a bi-fold's folded leaves), window (frame lines in the wall's place), opening (a gap with no symbol). A door's interval is the leaf's span, hinge jamb to the closing jamb the arc lands on; a window's is the frame's span.
method.window_rule: A window is a stretch of a wall where at least two thin frame lines run along it beside (or in place of) the wall's own line work: a frame rectangle or slider tracks. A bold stroke with one thin line beside it is a wall with its inner face, as the wall truth reads X8, X9 and X4 (method.judgement_calls of the wall truth); the top wall and the bay are single bold strokes with no window drawn.
method.profile_check: Every opening was read on 5-6x crops with a 10 px source grid (leaf, arc ends, jambs) and, for windows, on perpendicular ink profiles every 6-12 px along the wall (median of 3 columns, gray < 225, < 240 for the faint toilet-3 window); the readings are in each opening's 'method'.
method.ignore: An opening marked ignore is ambiguous in the drawing: the metric neither counts it as missed nor counts a detection on it as false.
judgement_calls: Window rule: only stretches with at least two thin frame lines beside or in place of the wall's line work are windows (G2-G4, G6). A bold stroke with one thin line beside it is read as a wall with its inner face, as the wall truth reads X8, X9 and X4; so the top wall, the bay and X4b (bold plus thin between the black piers) carry no window. The kitchen's X9b stretch y 461-548 has the frame box and sash (two thin lines beside the bold over y 505-545): window G6 (Task 17 review T1; first read as one outer line and left out).
G1, the living/balcony slider, is kind door, type sliding (Task 17 review T3): drawn with the window symbol (frame boxes and tracks) but it is the balcony's door; no hinge or swing is scored.

G5, G7 and G8, the balcony's edge B2 and sides B1 and B3, are drawn like window frames (bold plus thin lines, or thin pairs) but are railings: ignored (neither counted missed nor a detection on them counted false).
X6 (bedroom 3 over the 600 recess, faces 798.5 / 807.5) is a double-line wall, not an opening.

Door intervals span the leaf, hinge jamb to closing jamb: D1 and D2 (toilets) leave the 22-25 px above their hinges undrawn but outside the door; D6 (bedroom 3) starts below its 10 px nib under I8; D7 (entrance) ends at the hinge (y 778), above the corner stub.
D8 (store) is a bi-fold: one V of two leaves hinged at the upper jamb, folded toward -x.
